text: In 1930, buying a home looked like this.
You needed a big down payment.
The bank lent you the rest, for just five years.
Each month, you paid only the interest.
Then the whole loan came due, all at once.
Most people simply signed a new one.
Until the banks began to fail.
No new loan. The whole sum, due now.
At its worst, in 1933, around a thousand homes were foreclosed every day.
In 1934, the new Federal Housing Administration insured a different loan.
Long, and paid down a little every month.
No giant bill at the end.
Later, those terms stretched to thirty years.
That is still the standard American mortgage today.
